steps: This video shows when to split one request across specialist agents. A mixed ticket lands in TicketFlow: the customer was charged twice and the app crashes. Billing and technical, in one ticket.
First, a single agent handles both. It fixes the crash but loses track of the other sub-issue, and has to ask whether a refund was ever issued.
So you refactor. An orchestrator now decomposes the ticket into separable sub-tasks: the refund goes to billing, and the crash goes to tech.
It delegates both in parallel. The billing agent and the tech agent each get their own prompt, tools and model, working in an isolated context.
Each specialist works only on its own sub-task. Only the final results flow back to the orchestrator: refund issued, and root cause found.
The orchestrator merges both results into one reply to the customer. Nothing is dropped this time, and the ticket is resolved.

Multi-agent adds calls and hand-offs, so a small fix stays single-agent. The takeaway: split only when work is separable, overflows one context, or can run in parallel. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
